mainTopic: יעוד of an אמה העבריה: when it takes effect, whether the father can block it, and what the word ״לְאָמָה״ teaches
overview: The amud opens by finishing a proof: since יעוד works when a שוה פרוטה of the maidservant's time is left, קידושין can be done with a debt that has security. A ברייתא then teaches how יעוד is done. The תנא קמא says it works even at the last moment. רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה requires enough time left for a שוה פרוטה of work. רב אחא בריה דרבא shows that the ברייתא's משל of 'from now, after thirty days' fits the רבנן. A second ברייתא has רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה letting the father marry her to another man, and its 'after thirty days' משל fits him. A third ברייתא asks whether a father can sell his daughter on condition that there be no יעוד. רבי מאיר says yes, and חזקיה explains this from the word ״לְאָמָה״. The חכמים instead learn from ״לְאָמָה״ that a father may sell her to פסולים. רבי אליעזר finds that lesson in a different phrase and begins to give his own reading of ״לְאָמָה״, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Designation proves you can betroth with a debt that has security
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes its proof. יעוד works when a שוה פרוטה of the maidservant's time is still left, so in general קידושין can work with a debt backed by security.
steps.simpleTranslation: And when a peruta's worth of her time is still left and he designates her, it is a valid betrothal. Here too, it is no different.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a proof from the case of יעוד. It says that the same rule applies to the general case it was discussing before.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With יעוד, the master betroths the maidservant using the value of the work-time she still owes him, and she herself is like the security for that debt. Since that works, betrothing a woman with a loan that has security behind it should work too. The words הכא נמי לא שנא carry the rule over from יעוד to the general case.

keyTerms.meaning: He designates her (as a wife). This is the act of יעוד done to a Jewish maidservant.
Worth a פרוטה, the smallest amount that counts as value in halacha
Here too, it is no different. This phrase carries a rule over to a new case.
Betrothal

phrases.english: And when there still remains in her a peruta's worth
phrases.notes: He means a peruta's worth of work-time still left in her term as a maidservant.

phrases.english: and he designates her, it is a valid betrothal,
here too, it is no different.
phrases.notes: 'Here' is the general case discussed before this: betrothing with a loan that has security behind it.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי מְשַׁיַּיר בַּהּ שָׁוֶה פְּרוּטָה וּמְיַיעֵד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes an argument that started before this section
steps.raayaObject: Betrothing with a loan that has security is valid
steps.raayaSupportSource: The case of יעוד, which works when a שוה פרוטה of the maidservant's time is still left

steps.title: How designation is done, according to the first opinion
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא explains that יעוד is done by saying words of betrothal in front of two witnesses. The תנא קמא says it works even at the very last moment of her six years.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Sages taught: How is the מצוה of designation done? He says to her in front of two witnesses, 'You are hereby betrothed to me' or 'You are hereby engaged to me.' This works even at the end of the six years, and even close to sunset. From then on, he treats her as a wife and not as a maidservant.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that teaches how יעוד is done. It begins with the opinion of the תנא קמא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The master uses normal words of betrothal, and two witnesses must be present. The surprising point is the timing: even when almost no work-time is left, such as close to sunset on the last day, the יעוד still works. That suggests the betrothal does not depend on the value of the time that is left.

keyTerms.meaning: The מצוה of designating a Jewish maidservant as a wife
Two words that both mean 'betrothed'
The end of the six years of her service
Treating her as a wife
Treating her as a maidservant

steps.confusionAlert: 'Even close to sunset' is the key detail. Keep it in mind, because רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה will disagree with exactly this point.

phrases.english: The Sages taught:
How is the מצוה of designation done?
He says to her in front of two witnesses:
"You are hereby betrothed to me,"
or "You are hereby engaged to me,"
even at the end of the six years,
and even close to sunset.
phrases.notes: He means sunset on the very last day of her service, when almost no time is left.

phrases.english: And he treats her in the manner of a wife,
and he does not treat her in the manner of a maidservant.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a new source on יעוד itself
steps.mimraCoreRuling: יעוד is done with words of betrothal in front of two witnesses, and it works even at the very last moment of her service.

steps.title: רבי יוסי: enough time must be left for a peruta's worth of work
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה disagrees. יעוד only works if enough time is left in the day for her to do a שוה פרוטה of work.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי, son of רבי יהודה, says: If there is enough time left in the day for her to do a peruta's worth of work for him, she is betrothed. If not, she is not betrothed.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא brings a second opinion, which disagrees with the תנא קמא about timing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה, the betrothal 'money' is the value of the work-time that is still left. So if less than a שוה פרוטה of time is left, there is nothing to betroth her with. The תנא קמא does not require this.

keyTerms.meaning: Enough time

steps.whyThisMatters: This opinion shows what רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה holds the betrothal works through: only the work-time left at the moment of יעוד. The next steps depend on this.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei, son of Rabbi Yehuda, says:
If there is enough time in the day

phrases.aramaic: כְּדֵי לַעֲשׂוֹת עִמּוֹ שָׁוֶה פְּרוּטָה – מְקוּדֶּשֶׁת,
phrases.english: for her to do a peruta's worth of work for him, she is betrothed,
and if not, she is not betrothed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with the תנא קמא of step 2
steps.mimraCoreRuling: יעוד works only if a שוה פרוטה of work-time is still left in the day.

steps.title: The parable: betrothed 'from now, after thirty days'
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא gives a משל. A man betroths a woman 'from now, after thirty days,' and another man betroths her within the thirty days. She is betrothed to the first man.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is like a man who says to a woman, 'Be betrothed to me from now, after thirty days,' and another man came and betrothed her within the thirty days. She is betrothed to the first man.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא compares יעוד to a familiar case of betrothal with a delay. It is setting up a comparison that the גמרא will look at next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משל, the first man's betrothal reaches back to the start, so the second man's betrothal cannot take hold. Comparing יעוד to this case suggests that the maidservant's betrothal also goes back to the original purchase money.

keyTerms.meaning: A parable or comparison
From now, after thirty days. The betrothal is finalized later but counts from now.
To the first man

phrases.english: It is like one who says to a woman:
"Be betrothed to me from now
after thirty days,"
and another man came and betrothed her
within the thirty days,
in which case she is betrothed to the first man.

steps.triggerLanguage: מָשָׁל לְאוֹמֵר לְאִשָּׁה הִתְקַדְּשִׁי לִי מֵעַכְשָׁיו לְאַחַר שְׁלֹשִׁים יוֹם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא with a comparison
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A betrothal 'from now, after thirty days' takes hold for the first man, even if a second man betroths her within the thirty days.

steps.title: Whose opinion does the parable fit?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which of the two opinions in the ברייתא the משל matches.
steps.simpleTranslation: According to whom is this parable?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a clarifying question about the משל. This sets up the next steps, which test each opinion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא has two opinions but only one משל. The גמרא wants to know which opinion the comparison actually fits.

keyTerms.meaning: According to whom?

phrases.english: According to whom is this parable?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about the משל in step 4
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which opinion in the ברייתא the משל matches

steps.title: The parable cannot fit רבי יוסי
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא tests the idea that the משל fits רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה and rejects it. For him, the betrothal depends on the time left at the moment of יעוד, so it does not reach back to the start.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say the parable follows רבי יוסי, son of רבי יהודה, didn't he say that if there is enough time in the day for her to do a peruta's worth of work, she is betrothed, and if not, she is not?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries the first possible answer, רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה, and shows right away why it does not work.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משל, the betrothal reaches back to the very beginning. But רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה requires a שוה פרוטה of time left at the moment of יעוד, which shows that for him the betrothal only starts then. So his view does not match the משל.

keyTerms.meaning: If you say. This word introduces a suggestion that is about to be rejected.
But look, didn't he say

phrases.aramaic: אִילֵימָא מָשָׁל לְרַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה –
phrases.english: If you say the parable follows Rabbi Yosei, son of Rabbi Yehuda,
but didn't he say: if there is enough time in the day

phrases.aramaic: כְּדֵי לַעֲשׂוֹת עִמּוֹ שָׁוֶה פְּרוּטָה – מְקוּדֶּשֶׁת,
phrases.english: for her to do a peruta's worth of work for him, she is betrothed,
and if not, she is not!
phrases.notes: The גמרא is quoting רבי יוסי's words from step 3 back to show they clash with the משל.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִילֵימָא מָשָׁל לְרַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests the first possible answer to the question in step 5
steps.kashyaTarget: The suggestion that the משל follows רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה requires a שוה פרוטה of time left at the moment of יעוד, so for him the betrothal starts only then. The משל describes a betrothal that reaches back to the beginning.

steps.title: The משל matches the רבנן
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא בריה דרבא answers the question from step 5: the משל fits the opinion of the רבנן (the תנא קמא).
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא the son of רבא said: The parable matches the Rabbis.
steps.whatsHappening: After step 6 showed the משל cannot fit רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה, רב אחא בריה דרבא says it fits the רבנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For the רבנן, the sale of the girl works like a betrothal that takes hold later but counts from the beginning. That is just like 'be betrothed to me from now, after thirty days,' where the first man wins. So the משל fits the רבנן neatly.

keyTerms.meaning: The Rabbis, meaning the תנא קמא of the ברייתא
The parable matches (the opinion of)

phrases.english: Rav Acha the son of Rava said:
The parable matches the Rabbis.
phrases.notes: The Rabbis here are the first opinion in the ברייתא, the one that says יעוד works even at the last moment.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אַחָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרָבָא: מָשָׁל לְרַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Since step 6 ruled out רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה, this step assigns the משל to the רבנן.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whose opinion does the משל follow?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The משל follows the רבנן (תנא קמא).

steps.title: Isn't that obvious?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the ברייתא needed a משל at all if it plainly fits the רבנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: That is obvious!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא objects that this is too obvious to need saying, so why did the ברייתא bother with a משל?
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the רבנן already hold that יעוד reaches back to the sale, the matching parable seems to add nothing. The גמרא wants to know what new lesson the משל is teaching.

keyTerms.meaning: It is obvious; why say it?
A teaching of the תנאים not included in the משנה

phrases.english: That is obvious!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the need for the משל that step 7 just assigned to the רבנן.
steps.kashyaTarget: The need for the ברייתא to state the משל
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the רבנן's view already implies the betrothal reaches back, the parable seems unnecessary.

steps.title: The master never said 'from now'
steps.stepSummary: The משל is needed because one might think the master's case is different, since he never said 'from now.' The משל teaches that it counts as if he did.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have said: here he did not say to him 'from now.' So it teaches us that it is still like 'from now.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains what the משל adds. Without it, we might think the master's case is different from the parable.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the parable the man said 'from now,' but at the sale nobody said those words. We might have thought the master's betrothal cannot reach back. The משל teaches that the sale works as though 'from now' had been said, so the master wins.

keyTerms.meaning: You might have said (a mistaken first thought)
From now; the words that make a later betrothal count from the start
It teaches us (the real lesson)

phrases.english: You might have said,
here he did not say to him 'from now,'
phrases.notes: At the sale the father and master never used the words 'from now,' unlike the man in the parable.

phrases.english: so it teaches us.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַהוּ דְּתֵימָא, הָא לָא אֲמַר לֵיהּ מֵעַכְשָׁיו, קָא מַשְׁמַע לַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the 'obvious' objection of step 8.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Identifies a mistaken assumption the משל comes to prevent
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since the master never said 'from now,' his יעוד would not reach back to the sale.
steps.terutzMaskana: The sale is treated like 'from now,' just as in the parable.
steps.whatToRemember: For the רבנן, the sale of an אמה עבריה works like a betrothal 'from now,' so later יעוד reaches back to the sale.

steps.title: A second ברייתא: the father can marry her to another man
steps.stepSummary: Another ברייתא says that if a father sold his daughter and then betrothed her to someone else, she is betrothed to the second man. This is רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה's view.
steps.simpleTranslation: Another ברייתא teaches: One who sells his daughter and then goes and betroths her to another man has mocked the master, and she is betrothed to the second man. These are the words of רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ברייתא that discusses the same issue from a different angle. Here, רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה says the father can marry her off to someone else.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה, the master has no betrothal hold over her from the time of the sale. So the father's later betrothal to someone else takes effect, and the master is left out.

keyTerms.meaning: One who sells his daughter (as an אמה עבריה)
He mocked the master (took away what the master expected)

phrases.english: It is taught in another ברייתא:
One who sells his daughter,
and went and betrothed her to another man –
has mocked the master,
phrases.notes: The master could have married her through יעוד, and the father took that away from him.

phrases.english: and she is betrothed to the second man,
these are the words of Rabbi Yosei son of Rabbi Yehuda.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new ברייתא on the same dispute, starting with רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If the father betroths his sold daughter to another man, she is betrothed to that man (רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה).

steps.title: The חכמים: the master can still do יעוד
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים disagree: if the master wants to do יעוד, he can, and the second man's betrothal does not stop him.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the Sages say: If he wants to designate her, he designates her.
steps.whatsHappening: The חכמים give their side of the dispute in the second ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For the חכמים, the master's right to יעוד comes from the sale and reaches back to it. So the father's later betrothal to someone else cannot cancel the master's right.

keyTerms.meaning: And the Sages say (the opposing view)
To designate her as a wife through יעוד

phrases.english: And the Sages say:
If he wants to designate her, he designates her.
phrases.notes: 'He' is the master, and his יעוד wins over the second man's betrothal.

steps.triggerLanguage: וַחֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים: אִם רָצָה לְיַיעֵד מְיַיעֵד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposing view to רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה in the same ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The master may still do יעוד despite the father's betrothal to another man.

steps.title: The second ברייתא's משל: 'after thirty days'
steps.stepSummary: This ברייתא's משל: a man says 'be betrothed to me after thirty days,' and another man betroths her within the thirty days. She is betrothed to the second man.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is like one who says to a woman, 'You are betrothed to me after thirty days,' and another man came and betrothed her within the thirty days. She is betrothed to the second man.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא gives a parable to explain the dispute. This time the first man does NOT say 'from now.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: Without 'from now,' the first man's betrothal only starts after thirty days. By then she is already married to the second man, so the first man's betrothal never takes hold. This is the opposite result from the משל in step 4.

keyTerms.meaning: After thirty days, with no 'from now'
Within the thirty days

steps.confusionAlert: Compare carefully with step 4. There the man said 'from now, after thirty days' and the first man won. Here he said only 'after thirty days,' and the second man wins.

phrases.english: It is like one who says to a woman,
'You are betrothed to me
after thirty days,'
and another man came and betrothed her
within the thirty days –
she is betrothed to the second man.

steps.triggerLanguage: מָשָׁל לָאוֹמֵר לְאִשָּׁה הֲרֵי אַתְּ מְקוּדֶּשֶׁת לִי לְאַחַר שְׁלֹשִׁים יוֹם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds the ברייתא's parable for the dispute in steps 10–11.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Betrothal 'after thirty days' without 'from now' loses to a betrothal made within the thirty days.

steps.title: Whose opinion does this משל fit?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which opinion in the second ברייתא the 'after thirty days' משל matches.
steps.simpleTranslation: The parable: according to whom?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks whose view this new משל fits. This sets up the discussion that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא has two opinions but only one משל, in which the second man wins. The גמרא wants to pin down which of the two opinions this comparison actually fits.

keyTerms.meaning: According to whom?

phrases.english: The parable: according to whom?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks the same kind of question as step 5, now about the second ברייתא's משל.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which opinion, רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה or the חכמים, does the 'after thirty days' משל follow?

steps.title: The משל cannot match the רבנן
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא tests whether the 'after thirty days' משל fits the רבנן and rejects that idea, because the רבנן let the master do יעוד anyway.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say the משל follows the רבנן, that cannot be. The רבנן say that if the master wants to do יעוד, he may.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries out the first possible answer to its question, that the משל follows the רבנן, and right away pushes it away.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משל, the second man's betrothal wins and the first man loses. The רבנן hold the opposite in the maidservant case: the master can still do יעוד even after the father betrothed her to someone else. A משל where the second man wins cannot be the parallel for an opinion where the first man wins.

keyTerms.meaning: If you say, used to try out a possible answer
The Rabbis, the majority opinion
The master's designation of a Hebrew maidservant as a wife

phrases.english: If you say [the parable fits] the Rabbis,
but don't the Rabbis say:
if he wants to designate her, he may designate her!
phrases.notes: This is the חכמים's view from step 11. The master still wins even though another man betrothed her.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tries out and rejects the first possible answer to the question in step 13.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects matching the משל to the רבנן.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: In the משל the second man wins, while the רבנן let the first party (the master) win.

steps.title: The משל matches רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא בריה דרבא says the משל follows רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה, who holds the second man's betrothal works.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רב אחא בריה דרבא said: the משל follows רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה.
steps.whatsHappening: Since the רבנן do not fit, רב אחא בריה דרבא gives the answer: the משל matches רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה holds that once the father betroths his daughter to a second man, the second man's betrothal works (step 10). That matches the משל, where the man who betrothed her within the thirty days wins.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, which brings the real answer after a rejected one
A parallel case brought to explain a law

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא אָמַר רַב אַחָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרָבָא:
phrases.english: Rather, Rav Acha son of Rava said:
the parable matches Rabbi Yosei son of Rabbi Yehuda.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אָמַר רַב אַחָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרָבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the correct answer after step 14 rejected the רבנן.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The 'after thirty days' משל follows רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה.

steps.title: Isn't that obvious?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the ברייתא needed a משל at all if the comparison is plain.
steps.simpleTranslation: That is obvious!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא objects that this comparison is so plain that the ברייתא should not need a משל. It is setting up the explanation that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה already said clearly that the second man's betrothal works. Adding a משל that says the same thing seems to teach nothing new.

keyTerms.meaning: It is obvious, an objection that something says nothing new

phrases.english: It is obvious!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the need for the משל now that it has been linked to רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The need for the משל in the ברייתא
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה already ruled that the second man wins, a משל saying the same thing adds nothing.

steps.title: Why the משל is still needed
steps.stepSummary: Without the משל, one might think רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה ruled only because the master never said 'after thirty days.' The משל shows the second man wins even when a future time was set.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have said: here the master never told her 'after thirty days,' and that is the only reason the second man wins. The משל teaches us otherwise.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains what new point the משל adds.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One might think רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה lets the second man win only because the master never set a time for יעוד when he bought her. If he had said 'after thirty days,' you might think the master would win. The משל shows that even when someone says 'after thirty days,' a betrothal in the meantime still wins.

keyTerms.meaning: What might you have said? It introduces a mistaken first impression
It teaches us, the new point being made
After thirty days

steps.whatToRemember: The 'after thirty days' משל follows רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה. It teaches that a betrothal made in the meantime wins even over someone who set a future time.

phrases.english: You might have said,
here [the master] did not say to her
"after thirty days,"
phrases.notes: He means the master never set a future time for יעוד when he bought her, unlike the man in the משל.

phrases.english: so it teaches us [otherwise].

steps.triggerLanguage: מַהוּ דְּתֵימָא, הָא לָא אֲמַר לַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the 'obvious' objection of step 16.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows a new point the משל adds that would otherwise be unclear
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה ruled for the second man only because the master never said 'after thirty days.'
steps.terutzMaskana: Even if a future time had been set, a betrothal in the meantime wins.

steps.title: Selling a daughter on condition of no יעוד: רבי מאיר
steps.stepSummary: A new ברייתא: if a father sells his daughter on condition that the master will not do יעוד, רבי מאיר says the condition holds.
steps.simpleTranslation: Another ברייתא teaches: if someone sells his daughter and makes a condition that the buyer will not do יעוד, the condition stands. This is רבי מאיר's view.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ברייתא and starts a new topic: a sale made with a condition that blocks יעוד.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the father tries to block יעוד in advance through the terms of the sale. רבי מאיר says the condition works, so the master cannot do יעוד.

keyTerms.meaning: Stipulated, set terms
On condition that
Condition

phrases.english: It is taught in another baraita:
One who sells his daughter,
and stipulated on condition that [the buyer] will not designate her,
the condition stands,
these are the words of Rabbi Meir.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a new ברייתא on a related יעוד question.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי מאיר: a sale on condition of no יעוד is valid, and the condition holds.

steps.title: The חכמים: a condition against the Torah is void
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים say the master may still do יעוד, because a condition that goes against what the Torah says has no effect.
steps.simpleTranslation: The חכמים say: if the master wants to do יעוד, he may. The father made a condition against what is written in the Torah, and any condition against what is written in the Torah is void.
steps.whatsHappening: The חכמים disagree with רבי מאיר and give their reason.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Torah gives the master the right to do יעוד. A condition that takes away that right goes against the Torah, so it is cancelled. The sale still stands, but the master keeps his right to do יעוד.

keyTerms.meaning: He made a condition against what is written in the Torah
His condition is void
The Sages, the majority opinion

steps.confusionAlert: Only the condition is cancelled, not the sale. The sale still stands, and the master keeps his right to do יעוד.
steps.whyThisMatters: 'Anyone who makes a condition against what is written in the Torah, his condition is void' is a general rule that shows up in many places in ש״ס.

phrases.english: And the Sages say:
if he wants to designate her, he may designate her,
because [the father] made a condition
against what is written in the Torah,

phrases.aramaic: וְכׇל הַמַּתְנֶה עַל מַה שֶּׁכָּתוּב בַּתּוֹרָה –
phrases.english: and anyone who makes a condition against what is written in the Torah,
his condition is void.

steps.triggerLanguage: וַחֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים: אִם רָצָה לְיַיעֵד – מְיַיעֵד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposing opinion in the same ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: חכמים: the condition is void because it goes against the Torah, so the master may do יעוד.

steps.title: Does רבי מאיר really allow a condition against the Torah?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבי מאיר's view from step 18 using another ברייתא. There רבי מאיר says a condition against the Torah's marriage duties is void.
steps.simpleTranslation: Does רבי מאיר really say the condition holds? A ברייתא teaches that if a man betroths a woman on condition that she has no claim to food, clothing, and marital relations, she is betrothed and the condition is void. That is רבי מאיר's view. רבי יהודה says that in money matters the condition holds.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רבי מאיר's ruling from step 18. It points to a different ברייתא where רבי מאיר seems to say the opposite.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 18, רבי מאיר let a father's condition cancel יעוד, even though יעוד comes from the Torah. But in this ברייתא, רבי מאיר says a man cannot cancel the Torah's duties of food, clothing, and relations by a condition. That looks like a contradiction inside רבי מאיר's own view.

keyTerms.meaning: His condition stands (it works)
His condition is void (it has no effect)
Food, clothing, and marital relations: a husband's Torah duties to his wife
A money matter

steps.confusionAlert: Here רבי מאיר is the one who says the condition is void. רבי יהודה is the one who lets it stand in money matters. Don't flip them.

phrases.english: And according to Rabbi Meir, does his condition stand?
phrases.notes: This points back to the father's condition that the master will not do יעוד (step 18).

phrases.english: But isn't it taught in a baraita:
One who says to a woman: You are hereby betrothed to me
on condition that you have no claim against me
for food, clothing, and marital relations
she is betrothed,
and his condition is void; these are the words of Rabbi Meir.
Rabbi Yehuda says:
In a money matter, his condition stands.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי מאיר's ruling from step 18 using a contradicting ברייתא
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי מאיר's ruling that a condition against יעוד holds
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Elsewhere רבי מאיר voids a condition that goes against a Torah duty, so he should void this one too

steps.title: חזקיה: the word ״לְאָמָה״ makes יעוד optional
steps.stepSummary: חזקיה answers that this case is different. The פסוק says ״לְאָמָה״, which shows a girl is sometimes sold only as a maidservant, not for marriage.
steps.simpleTranslation: חזקיה said: It is different here, because the פסוק says ״לְאָמָה״, as a maidservant. That teaches that sometimes he sells her only as a maidservant.
steps.whatsHappening: חזקיה defends רבי מאיר. He shows that יעוד is not a fixed Torah duty, so a condition against it does not go against the Torah.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The contradiction only exists if יעוד is a Torah requirement. The word ״לְאָמָה״ shows the Torah itself allows a sale that is purely for service, with no marriage. So cancelling יעוד does not break anything the Torah demands, unlike food, clothing, and relations.

keyTerms.meaning: It is different here
As a maidservant
A maidservant

phrases.english: Chizkiya said:
It is different here,
because the verse says "as a maidservant"
sometimes he sells her
only as a maidservant alone.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in step 20
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishes the cases using a פסוק
steps.terutzHavaAmina: יעוד is a Torah duty, so a condition against it should be void, like the food and clothing case
steps.terutzMaskana: ״לְאָמָה״ shows a sale can be only for service, so יעוד is optional and the condition holds

steps.title: What do the חכמים learn from ״לְאָמָה״?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how the חכמים, who disagree with רבי מאיר, explain the word ״לְאָמָה״.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the חכמים, what do they do with this word ״לְאָמָה״?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sets up the next step. It asks what the חכמים, who do not accept רבי מאיר's use of the word, learn from ״לְאָמָה״.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Every word in the Torah must teach something. If the חכמים do not use ״לְאָמָה״ to make יעוד optional, they need another lesson from it.

keyTerms.meaning: The Rabbis (the חכמים)
What do they do with it? (How do they use it?)

phrases.english: And the Rabbis,
this "as a maidservant," what do they do with it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows from חזקיה's use of the פסוק and asks how the other side reads it
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What lesson the חכמים take from ״לְאָמָה״

steps.title: The חכמים: he may sell her to פסולים
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים use ״לְאָמָה״ for a ברייתא's lesson: a father may sell his daughter to people of flawed lineage.
steps.simpleTranslation: They need it for what a ברייתא teaches: ״לְאָמָה״ teaches that he may sell her to פסולים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question. The חכמים learn from ״לְאָמָה״ that a father may sell his daughter even to a man she could not properly marry.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For the חכמים, ״לְאָמָה״ is not about cancelling יעוד. It widens who the father can sell her to: even פסולים, since she is sold as a maidservant.

keyTerms.meaning: They need it (for a different lesson)
People of flawed lineage whom she should not marry
It teaches

phrases.english: They need this
for that which is taught in a baraita:
"As a maidservant" teaches that he may sell her to disqualified people.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 22
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: ״לְאָמָה״ teaches that a father may sell his daughter to פסולים

steps.title: Why need a פסוק? Logic should teach it
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא asks why a פסוק is needed. If a father may betroth his daughter to פסולים, surely he may sell her to them.
steps.simpleTranslation: But isn't this a logical argument? If he may betroth her to פסולים, shall he not be allowed to sell her to פסולים?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא challenges its own lesson. It argues that the rule could be learned by simple logic, so the פסוק seems unneeded.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Betrothal is a bigger step than selling her as a maidservant. If the father has the power to do the bigger thing with פסולים, he should be able to do the smaller thing. So why does the Torah need to say it?

keyTerms.meaning: But isn't it a logical argument? (We could learn it from reasoning)
He betroths her

phrases.english: But isn't it a logical argument:
if he can betroth her to disqualified people,
shall he not sell her to disqualified people?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The ברייתא challenges the need for the פסוק it just quoted
steps.kashyaTarget: The need for ״לְאָמָה״ to teach selling to פסולים
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A קל וחומר from betrothal should already teach the rule

steps.title: The logic fails: betrothal is broader than sale
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא rejects the logical argument. A father may betroth his daughter when she is a נערה, but he cannot sell her then, so betrothal shows broader power.
steps.simpleTranslation: What about betrothing her to פסולים? That is special, because a man may betroth his daughter when she is a נערה. Can we learn from it that he may sell her to פסולים, when a man cannot sell his daughter once she is a נערה?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא knocks down the logical argument from step 24. It shows the father's power to betroth is wider than his power to sell.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The argument assumed selling is the smaller power. But the father can betroth her even as a נערה and cannot sell her then. Since betrothal reaches further, we cannot assume what works for betrothal works for sale.

keyTerms.meaning: What about...? (opening a reason why one case is different)
A girl between twelve and twelve and a half
Since, because

phrases.english: What about betrothing her to disqualified people?
That is special, because a person may betroth his daughter
when she is a young woman,
so shall he sell her to disqualified people,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁאֵין אָדָם מוֹכֵר אֶת בִּתּוֹ כְּשֶׁהִיא נַעֲרָה?
phrases.english: when a person cannot sell his daughter when she is a young woman?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the logical argument of step 24
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The קל וחומר from betrothal to sale
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Betrothal is not the bigger power in every way. It works for a נערה, while sale does not.

steps.title: So the פסוק ״לְאָמָה״ is needed
steps.stepSummary: Since logic fails, the ברייתא concludes that the פסוק ״לְאָמָה״ is needed to teach that a father may sell his daughter to פסולים.
steps.simpleTranslation: Therefore the פסוק says ״לְאָמָה״. It teaches that he may sell her to פסולים.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא wraps up. Logic could not prove the rule, so the Torah had to write ״לְאָמָה״ to teach it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This confirms the answer in step 23. The חכמים have a real use for ״לְאָמָה״ that cannot be learned any other way. So for them the word is already taken by this lesson and cannot also teach that יעוד is optional, which is how חזקיה said רבי מאיר reads it.

keyTerms.meaning: Therefore the פסוק says (to teach what logic could not)

steps.whatToRemember: According to חזקיה, רבי מאיר uses ״לְאָמָה״ to show יעוד is optional, so a father's condition against it holds. The חכמים use the same word to teach that a father may sell his daughter to פסולים. A פסוק is needed for that, because betrothal and sale are not fully alike.

phrases.english: Therefore the verse says: "as a maidservant"
which teaches that he may sell her to disqualified people.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Concludes that the פסוק is necessary after the logic was rejected
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The חכמים learn from ״לְאָמָה״ that a father may sell his daughter to פסולים. Logic alone could not teach it.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר finds a different source for selling to people of flawed lineage
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר says there is no need for ״לְאָמָה״ to teach that a father may sell his daughter to פסולים, because ״אִם רָעָה בְּעֵינֵי אֲדֹנֶיהָ״ already teaches it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אליעזר says: If the point is to teach that a father may sell her to people of flawed lineage, that was already said in the words "If she is displeasing in the eyes of her master." This means she is 'bad' for marriage to him.
steps.whatsHappening: A new opinion in the ברייתא: רבי אליעזר argues that the lesson the חכמים learned from ״לְאָמָה״ is already found in a different part of the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אליעזר reads ״רָעָה״ ('displeasing') as 'unfit for marriage to him', meaning the master was not allowed to marry her. Even so, the sale was valid, so the Torah already shows that a father may sell her to a man she may not marry. That makes ״לְאָמָה״ free to teach something new.

keyTerms.meaning: 'It was already stated', meaning another פסוק already teaches this
'If she is displeasing in the eyes of her master' (שמות 21:8)
Her marriage

steps.confusionAlert: Here ״רָעָה״ does not mean the master simply dislikes her. רבי אליעזר reads it as 'her marriage to him is bad', meaning forbidden by lineage.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the key question for רבי אליעזר: if the lesson about פסולים already has a source, then ״לְאָמָה״ must be teaching something else.

phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer says:
If it is to teach that he may sell her to people of flawed lineage,
it has already been stated:
"If she is displeasing in the eyes of her master"
meaning that she is 'bad' in her marriage to him.
phrases.notes: So marriage to him was forbidden, and the sale still worked. That already shows a father may sell her to a פסול.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר: אִם לְלַמֵּד שֶׁמּוֹכְרָהּ לִפְסוּלִין, הֲרֵי כְּבָר נֶאֱמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disputes the חכמים' conclusion (Step 26) by giving a different source for the same law.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Selling a daughter to פסולים is learned from ״אִם רָעָה בְּעֵינֵי אֲדֹנֶיהָ״ (she is unfit for marriage to him), not from ״לְאָמָה״.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the need to use ״לְאָמָה״ for the law of selling to פסולים.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The חכמים' lesson is already covered by another phrase in the same פסוק.

steps.title: So what does the word ״לְאָמָה״ teach?
steps.stepSummary: Since the lesson about פסולים already has a source, רבי אליעזר asks what ״לְאָמָה״ comes to teach.
steps.simpleTranslation: What does the Torah teach by saying "as a maidservant"?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אליעזר asks the natural follow-up question. This sets up his own explanation of ״לְאָמָה״.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Torah does not use extra words for nothing. Once ״לְאָמָה״ is no longer needed for the law about פסולים, it must be teaching some other law, and the question asks what that law is.

keyTerms.meaning: 'What does the verse come to teach?', asked when a word seems extra
'As a maidservant' (שמות 21:7), the word under discussion

phrases.english: What does the verse come to teach by saying
"as a maidservant"?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows directly from Step 27: since ״לְאָמָה״ is now 'free', its purpose must be explained.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The lesson that ״לְאָמָה״ teaches according to רבי אליעזר.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר begins his answer
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר begins to explain that ״לְאָמָה״ teaches something about how a father may sell her. The sentence continues on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: It teaches that he may sell her...
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אליעזר starts his answer about what ״לְאָמָה״ teaches. The sentence is not finished here and continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The opening word ״מְלַמֵּד״ tells us a new law is about to be drawn from ״לְאָמָה״. It is a law about the father's power to sell, and the details come next.

keyTerms.meaning: 'It teaches', the usual opening for a lesson drawn from a פסוק
He sells her (the father selling his daughter)

phrases.english: It teaches that he may sell her
phrases.notes: The sentence isn't finished yet. The rest of רבי אליעזר's answer is on the next amud.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins answering the question of Step 28.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: ״לְאָמָה״ teaches a further law about the father's power to sell his daughter. The full answer continues on the next amud.
